Instead of tweaking prompts by feel, I scored them. Everything ran on a small local model (gemma3:1b) at temperature 0 with a fixed seed, so differences came from the prompt alone.

## Sentiment classification, 100 movie reviews

| Prompt                                 | Accuracy | Unparseable replies |
|----------------------------------------|----------|---------------------|
| Naive                                  | 0%       | 100                 |
| Structured (role, tags, output format) | 84%      | 0                   |
| Structured + few-shot examples         | 86%      | 0                   |

Always answering 'negative' scores 58%, so both structured versions are well above guessing. The naive prompt scored zero only because its replies could not be parsed.

## Other tasks

- Meeting summarization with action items
- Document QA with a refusal rule. A finding worth reporting: the model never refused either unanswerable question, with or without the constraint, so I documented the failure instead of hiding it.
- Jinja prompt templates rendered from JSON inputs
- A five-turn stateless shopping chatbot with automated checks on its replies
